Welcome! This guide is here to help you get the most out of SOGo Groupware — your open-source collaboration platform for email, calendars, contacts, and more. Whether you are setting up your SOGo 6 account for the first time or looking to master advanced features like shared calendars, Sieve mail filters, or resource booking, you have come to the right place. Every tutorial in this guide is built from real, step-by-step screen captures — so you see exactly what to click, type, and expect at each step. Screenshots reflect the SOGo 6 interface.

This tutorial walks you through creating a new event in SOGo 6's calendar, including setting the date and time, adding attendees, and configuring reminders.
A SOGo 6 account with valid credentials You are logged into SOGo 6

In the sidebar navigation on the left, click Calendar to open the calendar view. The calendar opens in Week view by default. You can switch between Day, Week, Month, and Year views using the buttons in the top toolbar.

There are three ways to create an event: Method Description Click the + button Click the + (plus) button in the top toolbar Double-click Double-click on any time slot in the calendar grid Use the date picker Click a date in the mini-calendar on the left, then click + Choose whichever method you prefer. A new event dialog will appear. Your browser does not support HTML5 video.

Fill in the event details: Field Description Example Event title A short name for your event "Team Standup" Calendar Which calendar to save to — chosen from your calendar list your personal calendar All day Toggle for all-day events (e.g., birthdays, holidays); the time fields are disabled — Start time / End time Date and time the event begins and ends Today, 10:00–11:00 Timezone (event) Time zone for start and end — useful when events span time zones GMT+01:00 Europe/Berlin Location Where the event takes place "Conference Room B" Description Notes, agenda or preparation instructions — URL Optional link (e.g., to the meeting document) — The dialog also has further fields that shape how the event appears to others: Field Options Effect Visibility Public · Private · Confidential Per-event classification — see Free/Busy: What Others See Show as Busy · Free · Out of office · Tentative How the event appears when someone checks your availability Status Confirmed · Tentative · Cancelled The event's own status Labels — Optional labels for the event Participants — Invitees — see the next step

If you want to invite other people: Click the Participants section to expand it Start typing a colleague's name or email address Select the person from the auto-complete suggestions Choose their participation role: Required — Must attend Optional — Welcome but not required Repeat for each additional attendee SOGo 6 will send an email invitation to each attendee when you save the event.
To receive a reminder before the event: Click Add reminder Set how far in advance you want to be reminded You can add more than one reminder per event.
Use the Description field to add notes, an agenda, or preparation instructions for the event. This field supports plain text.

For events that repeat, click the Repeat section and choose a pattern: Pattern Example Day(s) Standup meeting every day Week(s) Team meeting every Tuesday Month(s) Department meeting first Monday of each month Year(s) Birthday or anniversary You can also set an end date for the recurrence (e.g., repeat until the end of the semester).

Click Create Event to create the event (or Cancel to discard it). The event will appear on your calendar. If you added attendees, they will receive an email invitation that they can accept or decline.

You have successfully created a calendar event. You can now: Share your calendar with others Edit the event by clicking on it Drag and drop to reschedule Resize the event by dragging its edges to change duration

Check when your colleagues are available before scheduling a meeting — directly from the event creation dialog.

Free/busy data is not public. Availability is only shown for calendars that each attendee has actively shared — which is why sharing has to go both ways: You see colleagues only if they shared with you. A calendar without granted access renders as "No data" — their availability stays invisible. Colleagues see you only if you shared with them. The same check runs in reverse when someone else schedules the meeting. One-way sharing breaks the workflow. If only one side shares, every lookup in the other direction fails — the "Are you free at…?" emails come back exactly where free/busy was supposed to end them. Before relying on availability display, make sharing mutual — once: Share your own calendar — at minimum free/busy permission for your team Ask attendees to do the same That is why "No data" is not an error: it is the permission system working as intended.

Welcome! This page helps you get familiar with the SOGo 6 interface so you can start working right away.
Open your browser, enter your SOGo 6 instance URL (e.g. https://demov6.sogo.nu/SOGo/), type your username and password, and click Login. After successful authentication you'll see the main dashboard.

Once logged in, the SOGo interface is divided into three main areas: Top navigation — Module navigation: click to switch between Mail, Calendar, Contacts, and Tasks. Top toolbar — Module tabs, the three-dot menu (⋯), and your avatar (top right, for logging out). Main content area — Where the active module's content is displayed.

Click the three-dot menu (⋯) in the top toolbar to open your Preferences. Here you can configure language, time zone, notifications, default calendar view, email signatures, and more. Use the Green Save Button Always click the green Save button to confirm your changes. Preferences are not saved automatically — if you navigate away without clicking Save, your changes will be lost.
Click your avatar in the top-right corner of the toolbar and select Logout to end your session. See Logout for details.

This tutorial covers the basics of composing and sending emails using SOGo 6's webmail interface.
A SOGo 6 account with valid credentials You are logged into SOGo 6
In the sidebar navigation on the left, click Mail to open your inbox. Your inbox shows received messages in the main view, with folders (Inbox, Sent, Drafts, Trash) listed in the left panel.
Click the pen icon (Compose) in the toolbar above your message list. A new message composition window will open. Your browser does not support HTML5 video.

Fill in the recipient fields: Field Description To Primary recipient(s). Separate multiple addresses with commas or semicolons Cc Carbon copy — recipients receive a copy, visible to others Bcc Blind carbon copy — recipients receive a copy, hidden from other recipients Tips: Start typing a name — SOGo 6 will suggest matching contacts from your address book You can also enter full email addresses directly Use Cc for people who need to be informed but are not directly responsible Use Bcc for mailing lists or when recipients should not see each other

Enter a clear, concise subject line in the Subject field. tip Good subject lines help recipients understand the purpose of your email. Examples: ❌ "Meeting" ✅ "Sprint Planning — Tuesday 10:00" ❌ "Question" ✅ "Question about calendar sharing permissions"

Type your message in the large text area. Depending on your email editor settings, formatting options are available (such as bold, italic, and lists): Button Action B Bold I Italic U Underline Link Insert a hyperlink List Create a bullet or numbered list Attachment 📎 Attach a file To attach a file: Click the Attach button (paperclip icon) Select a file from your computer The file will upload and appear as an attachment in your message

If your message is time-sensitive, you can set a priority level: Open the three-dot menu (⋯) in the compose window Choose Priority and then the level you need (e.g., High or Low) — there is no separate Priority button High-priority messages will show a red exclamation mark ❗ in the recipient's inbox.
Once your message is complete: Review the recipient, subject, and content Click Send SOGo 6 will deliver the message. A copy is saved in your Sent folder.
If you are not ready to send: Click Save as Draft instead of Send The message is saved in your Drafts folder To continue later, open the Drafts folder and click the pen icon on the message to edit it
Check that To field has at least one valid recipient Large attachments may exceed server size limits (typically 25 MB) Check your internet connection
Verify the email address is correct The auto-complete searches your contacts, not the global directory Enter the full email address manually
You have successfully composed and sent an email in SOGo 6. You can now manage your inbox, organize messages into folders, and set up email filters for automatic sorting.

documents.t: SOGo 6 uses Sieve scripts for server-side mail filtering. Filters run when email arrives — before you see it in your inbox.
Click the three-dot menu (⋯) (Settings) in the top toolbar Select Mail → Filters Your browser does not support HTML5 video.

Choose when the filter should apply: Condition Example From contains @example.com → all mail from that domain Subject contains [Spam] → flag potential spam To contains team@company.com → mailing list messages Size larger than 5M → large attachments You can combine multiple conditions: All conditions must match (AND) Any condition can match (OR)

Choose what happens when conditions are met. Exact labels may vary slightly between versions — typical actions: Action Use Case Move to folder Sort into the right folder Copy to folder Keep a copy in inbox + file in folder Forward to Send to another address Mark as read Auto-archive newsletters Mark as flagged Highlight important senders Discard Delete spam (use with caution) Reject with message Bounce unwanted email with a custom message Important: Messages are only actually moved if you add Stop processing filter rules as the last action.
Filters run in order from top to bottom. Drag filters to reorder them. The first matching filter's action is applied.
Click Save or Apply. The Sieve script is compiled and activated on the server immediately.

Goal: Move all email from @company.com into the "Work" folder. Create the "Work" folder first (Part 1, Step 2) Open the filter settings → Create filter Condition: From contains @company.com Action: Move to folder → choose the "Work" folder Last action: Stop processing filter rules Click Save
Condition: Subject contains "URGENT" Action: Mark as flagged
Condition: From contains "newsletter@" Action: Move to folder "Newsletters"

Check that the filter's last action is Stop processing filter rules (see Step 4) Test with a simple filter first (e.g., move all mail from yourself) Whether Sieve is enabled (SOGoSieveScriptsEnabled = YES), which Sieve server address is configured, and whether server logs show Sieve compilation errors is part of the server configuration — that is your IT administration's job. Ask your administrator if in doubt.
Log out and log back in Check that the folder was created (not accidentally named with slashes)
Folders and filters help you maintain a clean inbox without manual effort. Start with 2–3 filters for your most common email patterns.

Configure automatic email replies and mark yourself as away in the calendar when you're on vacation or out of office.

A SOGo 6 account with valid credentials You are logged into SOGo 6 Vacation/auto-reply must be enabled by your administrator (SOGoVacationEnabled = YES — a server setting that is not visible to users; ask your administrator if in doubt)
Click the three-dot menu (⋯) (Settings) in the top toolbar Select Vacation from the settings menu Your browser does not support HTML5 video.

Field Description Example Start date When your absence begins 2026-07-15 End date When you return 2026-07-28 Time zone Your local timezone Europe/Berlin The auto-reply activates on the start date at 00:00 and deactivates after the end date at 23:59. tip Set the range to include travel days — enable it the evening before you leave and disable it the morning after you return.

Compose the message that will be sent to people who email you: Subject: Out of office — John Doe Thank you for your message. I am out of the office from July 15 to July 28, 2026, with limited access to email. For urgent matters, please contact Jane Smith (jane.smith@company.com). Best regards, John Doe

Option Description Send reply to Everyone, or only people in your contacts/address book Repeated replies Send once per sender (default) or every time they write Keep original subject Add Re: or keep the original subject line Recommended: Send once per sender to avoid flooding colleagues who email multiple times.
Click Save or Apply. The Sieve script — a server-side mail filter that applies rules to incoming email automatically — is activated on the mail server.
While you're configuring vacation, also block your calendar:

Open the Calendar module Create a new event covering your absence period Set it as an All-day event Add "Out of Office" or "Vacation" as the title Mark it as Busy or Out of Office in the visibility settings Save This blocks the time so colleagues see you're unavailable when checking free/busy.
Send an email to your SOGo 6 address from another account You should receive the auto-reply within a few minutes The auto-reply only fires once per sender (per configured rule)
Re-open Settings → Vacation to verify: The toggle shows ON Date range is correct Message is saved
When you return: Go to Settings → Vacation Toggle Enable auto-reply to OFF Click Save The auto-reply stops immediately. Optionally delete the calendar block event.

Check that vacation is enabled by your administrator Verify the Sieve server is running (SOGoSieveScriptsEnabled) The auto-reply only sends once per sender — test with a different email address Check that the date range includes the current date
The Sieve server may be unavailable Contact your administrator to check the Sieve service Simplify the message text (special characters can cause issues)
Vacation auto-reply ensures people know you're away without leaving them wondering. Combined with a calendar block, colleagues can see your availability at a glance.

SOGo 6 supports theme customization (light/dark mode) via user preferences.
